transcript.text: um ok so one instance I remember was during the Kanpur metro project when we had to decide whether to rush some finishing activities before quality checks because there was pressure to meet deadlines so some of the team members were in favour of just moving ahead but I felt quality could be compromised and it might backfire later so I brought it up in our meeting and convinced them to stick to the process even if it took a bit more time actually after discussing the risks everybody agreed and in the end the finishing came out well and we didn’t have to redo any work so that saved issues down the line
How would you set priorities when a project is behind schedule and several stakeholders want different things?
transcript.why: Your example showed the position you took, how you communicated the risk, and what resulted, so I moved to a broader prioritisation question.

transcript.text: um so basically whenever a project is behind schedule and stakeholders have different priorities I try to first understand which deliverables are actually critical for the overall timeline and which can be adjusted a bit so I speak to each stakeholder clarify what’s negotiable and try to make a list of the most urgent dependencies then I usually focus on tasks that are directly holding up other work or have the highest impact on project progress um I also try to communicate clearly about trade offs so everyone knows why some things get priority over others and I update everyone regularly if the plan changes
What would you examine first to decide which delayed activity should take priority?
transcript.why: Your answer described how you would compare urgency and dependencies, so I asked for the first thing you would examine when making that comparison.

transcript.text: um so firstly I would look at the project schedule and see which delayed activity is on the critical path because basically if something is delaying the critical path it directly impacts the whole project delivery so that would get top priority for me and then I’d also check which activity is a dependency for other teams or vendors to start their work so yeah critical path and then high dependencies are the first things I’d examine
If the activity on the critical path raised a significant safety concern, how would you decide whether to keep it as the top priority?
transcript.why: You identified the critical path and dependencies as the first checks. I’m asking how you would handle a situation where those priorities conflict with another important project consideration.

transcript.text: um actually if there’s a major safety concern even if it’s on the critical path I would not go ahead without resolving that issue first because safety has to come first no matter what the schedule is so I would immediately flag it discuss with safety officers and management and see if we need to stop work or put extra precautions in place so basically even if it delays the project a bit I’d rather be safe than risk an accident and then once the concern is addressed safely we can resume work and look for ways to recover time elsewhere
